# FIG. 5 - Second embodiment with a pulling element

**View:** Perspective view from above and to the front left, as FIG. 1. Outline line work only; the geometry carries no lettering, the numerals below being added in the annotation pass. The vibration motor and the air-extraction mechanism are omitted.

**Geometry to be drawn**

The covering element 36 is one large plain tile in perspective, as in FIG. 1, filling the lower drawing area. The machine stands on its right-hand part, with open tile to the left.

The machine and the tile are shown schematically, the machine as one plain rectangular body standing on a band that runs round its underside, the band alone touching the tile, these forms being a convention for this sheet only.

The band meets the underside of the body and follows the same rectangular run, its front surface facing the viewer as one unbroken strip across the whole width and drawn deep; its depth is schematic. It stands on the tile, its lower edge meeting the tile, and an open stretch of tile lies in front of the machine.

The rectangular body is drawn broad and tall, its front face turned toward the viewer as a large plain surface. The view being taken from the front left, the body's left-hand end is presented to the viewer and the body and band share one continuous outer edge on that side, while the right-hand end reads as one boundary edge only, running between the top face and the band.

The flexible pulling element 46 is drawn as one slack curved path in the manner of a loose cord, a single unbroken stroke carrying a heavy line weight, clearly heavier than the rest of the line work on this sheet, so that the path reads as a cord and not as an edge. It begins where it meets the left-hand side of the machine, that meeting place shown schematically with no attachment formation, and runs away to the left, sagging over the tile and stopping well inside the left-hand limit of the drawing area. From the machine to that stopping point it is one long, wide, gently curved sweep lying over open tile, crossing and touching no other line along the whole of that sweep.

The whole of the drawing stands well inside the drawing area.

- The vibration device 10 is the whole machine, the rectangular body with its band. Identified on the outer boundary line at the right-hand end of the body, clear of the flexible pulling element 46.
- The flexible pulling element 46 is that heavy curved stroke. Identified on the stroke itself, any point along the long sweep over the open tile being an equally correct endpoint, so that the leader ends on the drawn stroke and not on the tile beside it.
- The covering element 36 is that large plain tile. Identified well inside the open stretch of tile in front of the machine, clear of the flexible pulling element 46.
